Visit note | 2025-05-28 12:30 PM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Habiba Haque, 33, female. Mrs. Haque returns for review reporting persistent itchy eyes and symptoms that worsen noticeably when exposed to dust. She is a police constable and mentions her symptoms have grown worse since keeping a cat at home in Wari. She has no other chronic illnesses and denies fever or facial pain. On examination: about 12 sneezing fits a day, BP 118/85 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 66 kg. Nasal mucosa appears pale and boggy with clear secretions. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-05-28 03:00 PM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Prosenjit Mondol, 66, male. Mr. Mondol attends for follow-up, stating he gets tired easily and has experienced recurrent dizzy spells. He is a farmer and first noticed these sensations while resting after a family lunch in Rampura. He has no prior history of heart disease and takes no regular cardiac medications. On examination: pulse 132 bpm and irregular, BP 132/77 mmHg, weight 62 kg. Chest is clear to auscultation and heart sounds reveal an irregular rhythm. Assessment: Atrial fibrillation. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to limit tea and coffee, avoid alcohol, and report any fainting at once. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and kidney function tests.

Visit note | 2025-05-28 03:00 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Tamim Dewan, 56, male. Mr. Dewan presents for his first visit complaining of shaky hands, losing weight despite eating well, and a racing heart. He works as a call centre agent and first noticed the problem when his clothes became loose during a stay in Gazipur. He denies diabetes or prior thyroid disorders and has no heat intolerance other than mild palpitations. On examination: pulse 127 bpm, BP 136/74 mmHg, weight 76 kg. He was advised to avoid excess tea and coffee and rest when the heart races. Follow-up in 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.
